# Review

## I/O hardening (`io`) — pass

- `openSync` now uses `O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK`. On POSIX, a FIFO opened `O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK` returns immediately instead of blocking for a writer, and the subsequent `fstatSync` rejects it via `!stat.isFile()`. The no-wait FIFO requirement is met.
- The read loop fills a fixed `Buffer.alloc(65537)`; total bytes read can never exceed 65537 structurally, regardless of short reads. The post-fstat growth window is closed by the `offset > 65536` check after the loop, which catches growth even when the pre-read stat was ≤ 65536.
- `closeSync(fd)` runs in a `finally`, covering success and every failure path after a successful open; if `openSync` itself throws there is no descriptor to leak. Tests confirm closure by asserting `fstatSync(fd)` throws afterward.
- Positioned `readSync` calls are consistent (offset tracked manually), and a premature 0 read on a regular file leads to a JSON parse/canonical failure rather than silent acceptance.

## Authority preservation (`authority`) — pass

The only change to `readBinding` is the open flags and the read mechanism; `verificationObject`, `bindingRef === sha(data)`, canonical-form, scope, epoch, revision, inventory (`assertExecutorInventory` / digest comparison), `authorizeRead`/`authorizeStop` sync-grant wrapping, and the quiescence `recheck` transaction requirement are all untouched in the diff and the full module. No settle/release/replay path is introduced; the module still throws `CONTAINED_REOPEN_IS_NOT_RECOVERY_AUTHORITY` for any recovery commit and explicitly disclaims full-graph proof ("Per-invocation proof only").

## Tests (`tests`) — pass with one caveat

- Both stages (initial `reopen()` and final synchronous in-transaction `proof.recheck()`) are exercised for FIFO and growth; transaction rollback (`db.inTransaction === false`) and no-grant-consumption (`f.calls` unchanged) are asserted.
- The FIFO mock guard (`TEST_BLOCKING_FIFO_OPEN` when `O_NONBLOCK` is absent) makes a regression fail fast instead of wedging the Vitest worker — verified by the deterministic run showing old code fails these tests rather than hanging.
- Short-read coverage forces 97-byte chunks (asserts >675 reads) at the exact 65536 boundary, and the injected read-error test proves descriptor closure on the failure path.
- Mocks wrap `importActual` implementations, so real OS behavior runs unless a test deliberately interposes; the mock reset in `afterEach` is empirically safe (72 tests pass in order).
- **Caveat (warning, not blocking):** per the deterministic evidence, the two growth tests also reject on the old code — the post-growth `recheck` fstat sees the oversized file — so they do not independently isolate the new post-stat read cap. The cap is currently established by code structure plus the boundary test, not by a discriminating test. A variant that keeps later stat sizes plausible (e.g., grow to exactly 65537 bytes of valid JSON plus one trailing space, with `fstatSync` stubbed small throughout) would fail on old code for the right reason.

# Review

## io: pass
O_NONBLOCK lets the FIFO open return immediately and fstat rejects it via !isFile() — no writer wait. Reads are bounded by a fixed 65537-byte buffer, so actual bytes read never exceed 65537 even under short reads or post-fstat growth (offset > 65536 check closes the stat/read TOCTOU window). closeSync runs in finally; tests verify the descriptor is closed on success and on injected read error.

## authority: pass
Identity, canonical-form, bindingRef, scope/epoch/revision, inventory digest/assertExecutorInventory, and synchronous grant wrapping are unchanged; quiescence recheck still requires an enclosing transaction. No settlement, release, or replay path introduced; module still denies recovery authority and disclaims full-graph proof.

## tests: pass (one warning)
Both reopen and final in-transaction recheck stages are covered for FIFO and growth; exact-65536 boundary with 97-byte short reads (>675 reads asserted) and injected read-error closure tests are present. The FIFO mock guard converts a missing-O_NONBLOCK regression into a fast failure instead of hanging the runner, confirmed by old-code failures. Caveat: the growth tests also reject on old code (later recheck fstat sees the oversized file), so they do not independently isolate the new read cap — the cap currently rests on code structure plus the boundary test. A discriminating variant (grow to 65537 with stubbed-small fstat throughout, content valid JSON plus trailing space) would strengthen this.

judgments.summary: O_NONBLOCK prevents FIFO writer-wait; fixed 65537-byte buffer bounds actual reads under short reads and post-stat growth; finally-block closeSync closes the descriptor on success and failure, verified by tests.
Binding identity, canonical bytes, scope, inventory, grants, and transactional recheck logic are untouched; no settlement/release/replay introduced; module retains non-authority guard.

Both stages, exact boundary, short reads, and read errors are covered with real-OS-backed mocks and an anti-hang FIFO guard; however the growth tests do not independently establish the byte cap since old code also rejects via a later recheck stat.

findings.message: The post-fstat growth tests reject on the pre-patch code as well (a later recheck fstat observes the oversized file), so they do not by themselves prove the new post-stat read cap. The cap is currently supported by code inspection plus the exact-boundary short-read test.
findings.evidence: Deterministic run: 'Growth tests alone also reject in old code because a later read sees the oversized file; do not claim these two independently establish the byte cap.'

findings.message: FIFO rejection relies on POSIX semantics: O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK open succeeds immediately and fstat reports a non-regular file. Correct on POSIX; network-filesystem latency is explicitly out of scope per the task statement.

recommended_actions: Add a growth test variant where fstatSync is stubbed to report a small size throughout and the file grows to exactly 65537 bytes of otherwise-valid content (valid 65536-byte JSON plus one trailing byte), so the test fails on old code specifically because of the missing read cap.
